chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hammad ibn Ziyad, from Suleiman ibn Khalid
Regarding a man who cut the hand of a paralytic man, he (peace be upon him) said: Upon him is a third of the wergild.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: The blood money or financial compensation paid for injury or death.
key_terms.شَلَّاءَ: A person who is paralyzed or has a limp; specifically referring to someone with a pre-existing condition of the limb.

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for cutting the hand of a paralyzed person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of proportional compensation (diyah) for injuring a limb that is already impaired, specifically ruling that severing the hand of a person with paralysis (shalla') incurs one-third of the full wergild. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the actual functional value of the body part at the time of injury, distinguishing it from the compensation for a healthy limb. It serves as a foundational precedent for calculating damages in cases of cumulative or pre-existing physical disabilities.
